sources.fullCitation: Unsigned photograph. “MM. Chantrier et Nazelle, les auteurs du Fruit Défendu.” La Rampe (Paris), 9 January 1921, p. 12. Bibliothèque nationale de France / Gallica. ARK: ark:/12148/bpt6k55821649.
sources.title: MM. Chantrier et Nazelle, les auteurs du Fruit Défendu
sources.creator: Photographer uncredited
sources.researchNote: The photograph accompanies a notice of the operetta Le Fruit défendu at the Théâtre Cluny. The printed caption gives the lyricist’s surname as “Nazelle”; the person is René Nazelles.

media.title: Albert Chantrier and René Nazelles — La Rampe, 1921
media.altText: Black-and-white press photograph of two men in hats and overcoats standing at a café table, reading a sheet of paper.
media.publicCaption: Albert Chantrier and René Nazelles, composer and lyricist of Le Fruit défendu, photographed for La Rampe on the operetta’s run at the Théâtre Cluny. Nazelles went on to write French lyrics for Kaper.
media.publicCreditLine: Unsigned photograph, La Rampe, 9 January 1921, p. 12; Bibliothèque nationale de France, Gallica, ark:/12148/bpt6k55821649.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph appeared unsigned in a French periodical published on 9 January 1921 and is therefore an anonymous work, free in France seventy years after publication, that is from 1992. It was already in the public domain in its source country on the URAA date of 1 January 1996, so no United States copyright was restored, and a work published in 1921 is in any case out of copyright in the United States.
